disposition_reason: The results text prints one arsenic concentration (113 µg/L) and detection counts for arsenic, cadmium and lead in Chinese bai jiu; per-sample values are in an unavailable supplement.

study.origin: small production sites in rural Yunnan, Hubei and Anhui; small shops in Chongqing; a Beijing market; recorded comparison spirits from Beijing convenience stores
study.market: purchased from producers, shops and markets, China
study.method: nitric acid digestion with evaporation of alcohol, ICP-OES (PerkinElmer Optima 8300); results in µg/L
study.qa: calibration with national reference standard solutions; no CRM or recovery reported

findings.notes: Per-litre result kept unconverted. Only individually printed metal value; the authors note the maker was installing new equipment. Detection counts across 63 samples: arsenic detected in 29 (46.0%), cadmium in 47 (74.6%), lead in 38 (60.3%); all lead and cadmium below AMPHORA limits (10 µg/L Cd, 200 µg/L Pb). Per-sample values are in Supplementary Table S1 (not available).

unresolved: Per-sample metal results are only in Supplementary Table S1, which is not next to the PDF; only the single arsenic value printed in the text is extracted.
The abstract says one sample exceeded "100 mg/L of arsenic" while the results give 113 µg/L against a 100 µg/L limit; the text value is used.
Sample count: 56 unrecorded (9 Yunnan, 24 Hubei, 15 Anhui, 6 Chongqing, 2 Beijing) plus 7 recorded; detection percentages use 63.
Lead and cadmium were below AMPHORA limits but no concentrations are printed in the main text.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 100 µg/L; Cd 10 µg/L; Pb 200 µg/L

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Chinese limit for lead in grain bai jiu (GB 2762-2017)
